reason: E1 confirms NbMoTaW's room-temperature brittleness, and E2 shows that microstructural modification (continuous BCC matrix) improves ductility, but neither provides direct evidence that Ti addition enhances grain boundary cohesion or that minor Ti preserves high-temperature strength and irradiation resistance in this specific alloy.
premises: NbMoTaW is brittle at room temperature with negligible tensile ductility
Room-temperature brittleness in RHEAs can be attributed to a continuous brittle phase (e.g., ordered B2)
Ti addition can enhance grain boundary cohesion and disrupt brittle bonding networks
Minor Ti addition will not substantially alter high-temperature strength or irradiation resistance
A continuous BCC matrix with discrete second phases improves ductility while retaining strength
